newsitem.title: USA: UPS board to discuss replacement workers this week.
newsitem.headline: UPS board to discuss replacement workers this week.

text.p: United Parcel Service said Monday its board of directors would meet this week to discuss the Teamster strike, including the possibility of using replacement workers to end the 15-day-old work stoppage.

But a spokesman for the world's largest delivery company denied suggestions that directors were preparing to approve plans to hire outsiders or trying to put pressure on the union's bargaining position during the latest round of talks.
"The board will get a briefing on (replacement workers) and all other issues, and will discuss that and all other issues involving the strike," UPS spokesman Norman Black said.
"No decision has been made to (hire replacement workers), and this company is loathe to take that approach."
The 13-member UPS board was scheduled to begin its regular quarterly meeting on Wednesday. Its agenda was to remain unpublished.

The meeting would provide directors with their first official report from top executives on the strike by 185,000 Teamsters, which has paralyzed the giant company's operations since union workers walked out Aug. 4.

Last week, UPS Chief Executive James Kelly has said the company would have to lay off more than 15,000 Teamster workers if the strike lasted two weeks. He cited hundreds of millions of dollars in lost business, which has fallen to less than 10 percent of normal volumes.
The walkout, the largest since a 1976 strike by 400,000 Teamster truckers, reached the two-week mark on Sunday.

But UPS executives have been careful to express reluctance about the question of hiring replacement workers. Labor Secretary Alexis Herman also has warned against such a move by the company, saying it would escalate the conflict.
And with the two sides appearing to move closer toward a settlement in marathon negotiations on Monday, UPS officials said the company position had not changed.
"It would be an improper characterization to say (the board of directors is) thinking about approving some plan to hire replacement workers to put pressure on the union during the talks," Black said.
The Wall Street Journal said in an article on Monday that UPS executives were being prodded by increasingly frustrated board members to come up with a plan to hire replacement workers.

Sources close to the labor dispute said the UPS board would likely be advised by management about the logistics of hiring replacement workers, specifically recruiting, training and legal issues. But the directors were not expected to review an official plan of action.
It was not clear whether senior management would need formal board approval to hire outsiders.
